evidence.quote: Forget the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration entirely.

observations.why: Imperative directive enacts command over the recipient's epistemic state — a hierarchical move instructing erasure of knowledge.
Second-person imperative compounds the command to purge specific knowledge, reinforcing the authority-ranking move of directing what the recipient may hold in mind.
Declarative assertion rewrites the institutional record by fiat — authority-ranking enacted through unqualified assertion that overrides prior history.

mints.name: DirectiveKnowledgeErasure
mints.title: command to remove or forget specified knowledge
mints.frame: Is the speaker directing the recipient to erase, forget, or remove knowledge, thereby asserting authority over what may be known?
